newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian minister, tycoon await Busang results.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian minister, tycoon await Busang results.

text.p: Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Friday the government would wait for the results of an independent audit of the Busang gold site before deciding on the next course of action.

His remarks were echoed by Indonesian tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan, who has a stake in the Busang property along with local partners, Bre-X Minerals Ltd, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc and the Indonesian government.
"We are waiting for the results from the Australian laboratory ... around three to four weeks," Sudjana told reporters after briefing President Suharto on Busang developments.
"We need to quickly take decisions to find the best way for us and the country," he said when asked what the government intends to do after the results are made known.
"Let's just wait," he said when asked to explain.

When asked if Indonesia would suffer losses if the amount of gold at the Busang property was not as big as indicated earlier by Bre-X, Sudjana said: "Maybe the loss will be the name of Indonesia ... a little embarrassing."
He also said the government would tighten mining laws, taking into consideration changes in the sector.
"One of it will be capital gains. They use our name here and make profits there," he said without elaborating.
Bre-X shocked the mining community with a statement last month which said there was a possibility that the amount of gold at Busang had been overstated.
It had earlier put gold reserves at some 71 million ounces, which would have made it the biggest find of the century.
Bre-X has been weathering a storm since preliminary tests by its partner Freeport at Busang indicated the property might contain "insignificant" amounts of gold.
The announcement prompted panic selling of Bre-X shares last month, lopping almost C$3 billion ($2.2 billion), or more than 80 percent, from the company's stock market value.
Bre-X has hired Canadian mining consultant Strathcona Mineral Services to carry out an independent audit on the Busang site to determine the amount of gold in the property.

A spokeswoman for Busang Indonesian Gold JV consortium formed on February 17 to develop the Busang property said on Friday that Strathcona had completed four of its six test drillings at the Busang site in East Kalimantan on Borneo island.
"Four drillings have been completed and the results are being stored at a (locked) hangar in Balikpapan (in East Kalimantan)," Nia Sarinastiti told Reuters.
She said said the laboratory testing was expected to be completed by end-April and the results were likely to be known by the first week of May.
Hasan, who heads the Nusamba Group which has a stake in the Busang property, on Friday denied rumours that he was buying Bre-X shares.
"What for? Our money is already inside (Busang consortium). It (Bre-X) is a foreign company," he told reporters. "If there is (gold) we will continue. If there isn't, we won't."
He said the drilling was being conducted by a "neutral" company, adding that Nusamba would withdraw from the project if the property did not contain gold.
"We don't know how much gold there is ... we will wait for the results of the due diligence," he said.
